note: Parameters whose pooled value rests on a conversion factor from outside the source (a heating value, a density, a process ratio, a pooled efficiency, or an assumption), as examples so converted / examples pooled. Those values are shaded as converted in the workbook (see readme). Which factors: archetype-parameter.csv (external-factors); how each example was converted: example-parameter.csv (conversion, conversion-class, conversion-factors).

Parameters whose pooled value includes a figure the source prints wrongly and the modeller corrected (a slipped decimal or zero, a wrong unit or carrier label), as examples so corrected / examples pooled. Each correction, the figure as printed, and the evidence: records/reference/source-correction.csv; the rows carry the correction-id in example-parameter.csv (correction) and a note starting ASSUMED CORRECTION. These values are also counted in external-conversions and shaded as converted in the workbook (see readme).

Parameters with no sourced value, filled by the fill step and graded: identity (calculated from this archetype's own values), estimated (from other archetypes or a class rule fitted on this database), proxy (a class constant from a named outside catalogue, records/fill/fill-assumption.csv) or guess (a judgement, records/fill/fill-judgement.csv); not-applicable marks a parameter that does not characterise the archetype. Shaded by grade in the workbook (see readme); their _n is 0. Rule, inputs, and rationale: archetype-parameter.csv (grade, method, rule-id, inputs, rationale); rules in records/fill/.
Expected technical service life of the installed equipment.

The unit the capacity columns are in, chosen per archetype as the unit its industry rates plants in (records/reference/capacity-unit.csv). Not the product-unit: annual output and the per-capacity costs stay per product-unit.
Rated (nameplate) capacity of one unit: the most it can make running flat out, on the basis named in capacity-basis. A rate, not what the unit makes; see annual-output.
Annual output as a fraction of output at rated capacity running continuously.
Useful output of one unit over a typical year: capacity x capacity-factor. In the database's units, MW x 31,536 GJ/yr per MW, or kt/yr x 1000 t per kt, times the capacity factor.

Useful output per unit of energy input, on a higher heating value (HHV) basis: a source's LHV figure is converted with the heating values of the fuel in and the product out (pipeline/heating.py). For multi-carrier technologies record one tech-flow row per input instead. On CHP archetypes (label says CHP) this column is the total CHP efficiency, electricity plus useful heat over fuel in (efficiency-chp); the electric and heat efficiencies are beside it.

Useful output per unit of energy input, on a higher heating value (HHV) basis: a source's LHV figure is converted with the heating values of the fuel in and the product out (pipeline/heating.py). For multi-carrier technologies record one tech-flow row per input instead. Species or stream: electricity. Electricity out over energy in. On a single-output power archetype it repeats the efficiency column.

Useful output per unit of energy input, on a higher heating value (HHV) basis: a source's LHV figure is converted with the heating values of the fuel in and the product out (pipeline/heating.py). For multi-carrier technologies record one tech-flow row per input instead. Species or stream: heat. Heat out over energy in. On a single-output heat archetype it repeats the efficiency column.
Useful heat output per unit of electricity output for a CHP unit.
Total final energy input per unit of product output, all carriers, on a final-energy basis.
Temperature of the delivered heat. Governs tier assignment. Low and high also span the minimum and maximum operating temperatures sources give (temperature-min, temperature-max).
Pressure of delivered steam. Record the source's own unit.

Percentage of the hours in a year the unit is ABLE to run, after planned and unplanned outages. It is a property of the equipment, not of how it is operated: capacity-factor is what it actually produced, and is bounded above by this. A boiler at 90% availability and a 60% capacity factor was available for 90% of the year and run for 60% of it.
Overnight capital cost per unit of capacity, on the basis named in cost-basis.
Annual operating and maintenance cost that does not vary with output.
Operating cost per unit of output, excluding purchased energy and feedstock.

Fixed and variable operating cost reported TOGETHER, where the source does not split them. Say in the row note exactly what it includes - sources differ on whether fuel, electricity, materials, and depreciation are inside. Never record an opex-fixed or opex-variable on top of an opex-total for the same technology and source.

Cost per unit of product or service including capital recovery, as the source reports it: a levelized cost of electricity, heat, hydrogen, or product, a production cost, or a cost per tonne of CO2 captured, transported, or stored. NOT a capex or opex and never pooled with one; it depends on the source's discount rate, fuel prices, and capacity factor, which its note records (discount-rate is recorded as its own parameter where printed). Added 2026-09-25; loaded from main files and from the sidecars that held levelized costs, 2026-09-26.

Cost per unit of product or service including capital recovery, as the source reports it: a levelized cost of electricity, heat, hydrogen, or product, a production cost, or a cost per tonne of CO2 captured, transported, or stored. NOT a capex or opex and never pooled with one; it depends on the source's discount rate, fuel prices, and capacity factor, which its note records (discount-rate is recorded as its own parameter where printed). Added 2026-09-25; loaded from main files and from the sidecars that held levelized costs, 2026-09-26. Species or stream: calculated.

Cost per unit of product or service including capital recovery, as the source reports it: a levelized cost of electricity, heat, hydrogen, or product, a production cost, or a cost per tonne of CO2 captured, transported, or stored. NOT a capex or opex and never pooled with one; it depends on the source's discount rate, fuel prices, and capacity factor, which its note records (discount-rate is recorded as its own parameter where printed). Annualization factor applied to capex. Record the source study's own factor, not the model's.
Financial rate used by the source when levelizing. Recorded so a levelized cost can be inverted without double-counting the model's own hurdle rate.
Years from investment decision to commissioning.
Fractional capex reduction per doubling of cumulative installed capacity.

Emissions from burning fuel at the technology, per unit of energy input or product output. Species named in target. Excludes the process reaction, which is emissions-process, and excludes purchased energy, which is out of scope. Species or stream: co2e.
Emissions from the chemical reaction rather than fuel combustion, per unit of product. Species or stream: co2e.

Combustion plus process emissions together, per unit of product, where a source reports only the combined figure. Scope 1. NEVER record this alongside emissions-combustion and emissions-process for the same technology and source - it is the sum of them, and the three together double count. Species or stream: co2e.

Fraction of the CO2 entering the capture plant that it captures. Recorded on capture plants (the co2-capture family) only. The plant-level capture rate is share-to-capture on the host times this, and is not recorded directly. Species or stream: co2.

Fraction of the host plant's CO2 sent to the capture plant. Recorded on host plants with capture. Times the capture plant's capture-rate it gives the plant-level capture rate; where a source gives only the plant-level rate, that rate is recorded here. Species or stream: co2.

Cost of avoiding one tonne of CO2-eq by using this technology instead of the incumbent, as the source reports it. NOT a capital or operating cost and never interchangeable with one: it already nets the technology's costs against the incumbent's and divides by the emissions avoided, so the incumbent it was measured against belongs in the note. Added 2026-08-29 for IPCC AR6 Chapter 11 Table 11.3, which reports costs only in this form.

Reduction in GHG emissions this option can deliver relative to current practice, as a percentage. A ceiling on what the option can do, not a projection of what it will do. Where a source says these are multiplicative rather than additive across options -- as IPCC AR6 Table 11.3 does -- they must not be summed.

Biogenic CO2 released at the technology per unit of product: from biomass fuels (black liquor, wood, biogas) or carbonate whose carbon came from biomass (kraft lime mud). Not part of emissions-combustion, emissions-process, or emissions-total, which are fossil (ruling 2026-10-14). Species or stream: co2.
Emissions captured rather than released, per unit of energy input or product output. Species named in target. The counterpart of capture-rate as an absolute quantity. Species or stream: co2.
